subject: Latent and Manifest variable cross lagged

messages.author: 56e14d36ffa830a3
messages.subject: Latent and Manifest variable cross lagged
parts:
Hello,

I have three variables x, y, Z; x and y are latent while Z is observable variable. I want to do cross lagged analysis among the three variables. Is this the right model specification?
model<- ' x1=~ xa1 + xb1
              x2=~ xa2 + xb2
              x3=~ xa3 + xb3

              y1=~ ya1 + yb1
              y2=~ ya2 + yb2
              y3=~ ya3 + yb3
              
           x2 ~ x1 + y1 + Z1
           x3 ~ x2 + y2 + Z2 + x1

           y2 ~ x1 + y1  + Z1
          y3 ~ x2 + y2+ Z2 + y1

         Z2 ~ x1 + y1  + Z1
         Z3 ~ x2 + y2 + Z2 + Z1

         x1 ~~ y1 + Z1
         x2 ~~y2 + Z2
        x3 ~~y3 + Z3
        y1~~ Z1
        y2 ~~ Z2
        y3 ~~ Z3'

fit3<- sem(model, data=sr, missing="pairwise", estimator="WLSMV", 
           ordered =c("xa1", "xb1",  "xa2", "xb2","xa3", "xb3",
                           ya1", "yb1",  "ya2", "yb2","ya3", "yb3"))

PS: the latent variable are measured by ordinal items (xa1, xb1 ....). I will look forward to your suggestions. 

Best regards,
Ashenafi

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Latent and Manifest variable cross lagged
parts:
Wait, fixed.x=FALSE will not work, since you are using estimator="WLSMV".

Then, they only thing you can do (to allow for a correlation between Z3
and x3, y3) is to 'upgrade' Z3 to a latent variable:

Put this at the top of your syntax:

fZ3 =~ 1*Z3
Z3 ~~ 0*Z3

AND

replace all occurrences of 'Z3' by 'fZ3', which is now treated as a
stochastic variable.

Yves.
